title: Mechanics: Forces and Motion - Practice Exam
instructions: Answer all questions. Multiple-choice questions have four options (A, B, C, D). Show all work for free-response questions.

questions.question: A 4 kg object is pushed across a frictionless surface with a net force of 16 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Using Newton's second law: F = ma, so a = F/m = 16 N / 4 kg = 4 m/s²

questions.question: At the maximum height of a projectile's trajectory, which statement is true?
options: Vertical velocity is zero, but horizontal velocity is not zero
Horizontal velocity is zero, but vertical velocity is not zero
Both vertical and horizontal velocities are zero
Both vertical and horizontal velocities remain constant
questions.explanation: At maximum height, the vertical component of velocity momentarily becomes zero as the projectile stops rising. However, the horizontal component continues unchanged throughout the flight.

questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 5 seconds. What distance does it travel?
questions.explanation: Using s = ½(v₀ + v)t = ½(0 + 20)(5) = ½(20)(5) = 50 m. Or using s = v₀t + ½at²: a = 20/5 = 4 m/s², so s = 0 + ½(4)(25) = 50 m.

questions.question: Two forces act on an object: 3 N due east and 4 N due north. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.explanation: For perpendicular forces, R = √(F₁² + F₂²) = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 N

questions.question: According to Newton's third law, action and reaction forces:
options: Act on the same object and cancel each other
Act on different objects and are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction
Are only present when an object is accelerating
Only occur in the absence of friction
questions.explanation: Action-reaction pairs act on different objects, are equal in magnitude, and are opposite in direction. They do not cancel because they act on different objects.

questions.question: A projectile is launched at 50 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. What is the horizontal component of its initial velocity?
questions.explanation: The horizontal component is vₓ = v₀ cos θ = 50 cos(30°) = 50 × (√3/2) = 25√3 ≈ 43.3 m/s

questions.question: An object is in equilibrium. Which of the following must be true?
options: The net force on the object is zero
The object is moving at constant velocity only
The object must have zero mass
questions.explanation: Equilibrium means the net force is zero. An object in equilibrium may be at rest OR moving at constant velocity (Newton's first law).

questions.question: True or False: Inertia is a force that opposes motion.
questions.explanation: Inertia is not a force; it is a property of matter representing resistance to changes in motion. Friction is a force that opposes motion.

questions.question: True or False: In free fall, an object dropped from rest will have zero velocity at any point during its fall.
questions.explanation: An object dropped from rest has zero velocity only at the moment of release. After that, it accelerates due to gravity and gains velocity continuously.

questions.question: True or False: The horizontal velocity of a projectile changes during its flight due to gravity.
questions.explanation: Gravity acts vertically, not horizontally. The horizontal velocity of a projectile remains constant throughout its flight (ignoring air resistance).

questions.question: A 6 kg object is pushed with a net force of 30 N. Its acceleration is ________ m/s².
questions.explanation: Using F = ma: a = F/m = 30/6 = 5 m/s²

questions.question: A 50 N force is applied 2 m from a pivot. The torque produced is ________ N·m.
questions.explanation: Using τ = F × d: τ = 50 × 2 = 100 N·m

questions.question: A ball is thrown horizontally from a cliff with a velocity of 12 m/s. At maximum height (the launch point), what is the magnitude of its velocity? Explain why.
questions.correctAnswer: 12 m/s (horizontal); At the launch point, the vertical velocity is zero, leaving only the horizontal component of velocity.

questions.question: Explain why action-reaction pairs do not cancel each other according to Newton's third law.
questions.correctAnswer: Action-reaction pairs act on different objects. Since they act on different objects, neither force contributes to the net force on any single object, so they cannot cancel each other.
